title: Cup Cap Cross Products and Cohomology Rings

items.title: Alexander--Whitney map and diagonal approximation
items.statement: For spaces X,Y and a commutative unital ring R, AW:C_n(X times Y;R) to direct-sum_{p+q=n} C_p(X;R) tensor_R C_q(Y;R) sends sigma to sum_{p=0}^n (pr_X sigma)|[v_0,...,v_p] tensor (pr_Y sigma)|[v_p,...,v_n]. The diagonal approximation is D_X=AW composed with Delta_#. Empty spaces and the zero ring give the zero map.
items.strategy: This is the front/back-face formula. Expanding the alternating boundary makes all middle cuts cancel and leaves the signed tensor differential, so AW and D_X are chain maps. Postcomposition on faces proves naturality.

items.title: Alexander--Whitney and shuffle are natural chain-homotopy inverses
items.statement: The Alexander--Whitney map AW and signed shuffle S are natural chain maps over every commutative unital ring R; AW S and S AW are naturally chain homotopic to the identities and preserve degree-zero augmentation. No AC is required.
items.strategy: The prerequisite shuffle comparison supplies a specified natural inverse T and homotopies using fixed contractions of simplex models. AW and T agree in degree zero. Inductively, the difference on the universal n-simplex minus the already-built lower homotopy is an augmentation-zero cycle; the fixed model contraction fills it, giving AW~T naturally. Compose with TS~1 and ST~1, then extend scalars to R.

items.title: Singular cup product on cochains
items.statement: Let R be a commutative unital ring and delta phi=phi boundary. For phi in C^p(X;R), psi in C^q(X;R), define (phi cup psi)(sigma)=phi(sigma|[v_0,...,v_p]) psi(sigma|[v_p,...,v_{p+q}]). Equivalently this is diagonal pullback of the additive external product through AW. No multiplication is assigned to coefficients in a bare abelian group.
items.strategy: Evaluate AW in bidegree (p,q); all other cuts vanish by degree. R-bilinearity uses the specified multiplication R tensor R to R. This fixes the positive-differential convention with no extra cochain-cross-product sign.

items.title: Cup product Leibniz identity
items.statement: For phi in C^p(X;R) and psi in C^q(X;R), delta(phi cup psi)=delta phi cup psi+(-1)^p phi cup delta psi. Thus cocycles multiply and changing either representative changes the product by a coboundary.
items.strategy: Apply the AW chain-map identity and evaluate the signed tensor differential. Expand representative changes and use the identity twice, including delta a cup delta b=delta(a cup delta b), to exhibit every extra term as a coboundary.

items.title: Singular cohomology ring
items.statement: For a space X and commutative unital ring R, H^*(X;R)=direct-sum_{n>=0}H^n(X;R), with [phi][psi]=[phi cup psi], is the singular cohomology graded ring. Its unit is the class of the zero-cochain taking value 1 on every singular vertex in every component.
items.strategy: Leibniz gives descent. The proposed unit is closed because it agrees on the endpoints of every edge, and the front/back formula makes it a two-sided unit.

references.title: Hatcher §3.2, The Cohomology Ring; Miller Definition 29.1

items.title: Cup product is natural, unital and associative
items.statement: For continuous f:X to Y, f^*(a cup b)=f^*a cup f^*b and f^*(1)=1. Cup is associative already on cochains, so f^* is a unital graded-ring homomorphism.
items.strategy: Postcomposition commutes with every face. Both parenthesizations evaluate the three factors on vertex blocks 0..p, p..p+q, and p+q..p+q+r, proving strict associativity. The unit calculation is immediate.

items.title: Factor reversal gives the commutativity chain homotopy
items.statement: Let tau interchange X times X and T(a tensor b)=(-1)^{pq}b tensor a in bidegree (p,q). The natural chain maps T AW tau_# and AW are naturally chain homotopic. Their composites with Delta_# are therefore naturally chain homotopic. No AC is required.
items.strategy: T is a chain map by the signed tensor differential, and shuffle naturality gives tau_#S=ST. Hence AW and TAWtau_# are augmentation-preserving homotopy inverses of S. The fixed simplex-model contraction induction fills their difference in each degree, producing the natural homotopy; precompose with Delta_#.

references.title: Hatcher proof of Theorem 3.11; Miller Lecture 29

items.title: Singular cohomology is graded commutative
items.statement: For a in H^p(X;R), b in H^q(X;R) over a commutative unital ring, a cup b=(-1)^{pq}b cup a. The defining cochain operation need not be graded commutative.
items.strategy: Evaluate cocycles on the two homotopic diagonal approximations. The tensor twist contributes (-1)^{pq}; evaluation on a chain homotopy differs by a coboundary, so equality holds on classes.

items.title: Relative cup product for an excisive triad
items.statement: For subspaces A,B of X, the front/back formula sends C^p(X,A;R) tensor C^q(X,B;R) to cochains vanishing on C_*(A)+C_*(B). If A and B are open and cover A union B (or a stated neighborhood/subcomplex replacement gives this chain comparison), small-chain excision identifies the target with H^{p+q}(X,A union B;R), defining the relative cup product. A hypothesis is necessary because a simplex in A union B need not lie wholly in either member.
items.strategy: A simplex wholly in A kills the first factor and one wholly in B kills the second. Leibniz gives descent for C_*(A)+C_*(B). Subdivide chains subordinate to the two-open cover; the small-chain inclusion is a chain-homotopy equivalence, identifying that sum with chains on A union B. No arbitrary-triad claim is made.

references.title: Hatcher relative products after Proposition 3.10; Miller Lecture 34

items.title: Relative cup products are natural and connector-compatible
items.statement: For maps of excisive triples, relative cup products are natural. If d is the cohomology connector, x has degree p, and restrictions make the products meaningful, d(x cup i^*y)=d(x) cup y and d(i^*x cup y)=(-1)^p x cup d(y), using the positive coboundary and displayed factor order.
items.strategy: Use cochain lifts in the short exact relative-cochain sequences. Apply delta and Leibniz: the first closed factor leaves no sign and the second connector crosses a degree-p factor, producing (-1)^p. These lifted coboundaries define the connectors. Naturality is termwise, and small-chain comparison transports the identities.

references.title: Hatcher relative cup products; Miller Lecture 34

items.title: Cap product with cohomology written first
items.statement: For phi in C^p(X;R) and an n-simplex sigma with n>=p, phi cap sigma=phi(sigma|[v_0,...,v_p]) sigma|[v_p,...,v_n], extended R-bilinearly and zero for n<p. Cohomology is written first; evaluation uses the front face and retains the back face.
items.strategy: This is the (p,n-p) component of the AW diagonal followed by evaluation in the first tensor factor. Fixing the order here fixes all later signs.

items.title: Cap product boundary identity
items.statement: For phi in C^p(X;R) and c in C_n(X;R), boundary(phi cap c)=(-1)^p(phi cap boundary c-delta phi cap c). Therefore cap descends to H^p(X;R) tensor H_n(X;R) to H_{n-p}(X;R).
items.strategy: Expand the retained back-face boundary. Internal faces match phi cap boundary c; the omitted first back face is the final face in delta phi with the displayed sign. Regroup, then apply the identity to cycles, boundaries, cocycles and coboundaries.

references.title: Hatcher cap boundary formula p.239; Miller Lecture 34

items.title: Cap naturality and projection formula
items.statement: For f:X to Y, f_*(f^*alpha cap x)=alpha cap f_*x. Also (alpha cup beta) cap x=beta cap(alpha cap x) under the cohomology-first convention.
items.strategy: Postcomposition commutes with front/back restrictions. Both projection-formula sides evaluate alpha on 0..p, beta on p..p+q, retain p+q..n, and multiply in the same order. Boundary identity gives descent.

items.title: Relative cap products with quotient domains displayed
items.statement: For subspaces A,B of X the chain formula induces C^p(X,A;R) tensor C_n(X)/(C_n(A)+C_n(B)) to C_{n-p}(X,B;R). Under the excisive hypotheses of the relative cup definition this gives H^p(X,A) tensor H_n(X,A union B) to H_{n-p}(X,B), including H^p(X,A) tensor H_n(X,A) to H_{n-p}(X) and H^p(X,A) tensor H_n(X) to H_{n-p}(X,A).
items.strategy: Chains in B retain a back face in B; chains in A evaluate to zero. Thus both quotient relations are respected. The boundary identity proves descent, and the same small-chain comparison replaces the sum by A union B only under the stated hypotheses.

references.title: Hatcher relative cap products pp.239--241; Miller Lecture 34

items.title: Cohomological Kunneth cross product is a ring isomorphism
items.statement: Assume AC and exactly the finite-free hypotheses of the additive cohomological Kunneth theorem over R. External product is an isomorphism H^*(X;R) graded-tensor_R H^*(Y;R) to H^*(X times Y;R), with (a tensor b)(a' tensor b')=(-1)^{|b||a'|}(a cup a') tensor (b cup b'). For CW pairs the same proof gives H^*(X,A) tensor H^*(Y,B) isomorphic to H^*(X times Y,A times Y union X times B) when one relative factor is finite free degreewise. Multiplicativity is choice-free; AC is inherited only for additive bijectivity.
items.strategy: Compare AW cuts on X times Y with the factor cuts. Moving b past a' contributes the Koszul sign; units correspond to 1 tensor 1. Invoke the prerequisite theorem only for absolute additive bijectivity. For pairs, first treat B empty with the same relative cochain argument, then collapse B and use the split pair/triple exact sequences plus the five lemma, as in Hatcher Theorem 3.18. This identifies the exact AC use.

references.title: Hatcher Theorems 3.15 and 3.18; Miller Proposition 29.2 and Theorem 33.3

items.title: Cup length over a coefficient ring
items.statement: For nonempty X and commutative unital R, cup-length_R(X) is the supremum in nonnegative integers union {infinity} of k for which positive-degree reduced classes a_1,...,a_k have nonzero product. It is 0 if none exists and infinity if lengths are unbounded.
items.strategy: The supremum convention covers absence of a largest finite length. Positive degree prevents unit-padding, and ring naturality gives homotopy invariance.

items.title: Positive-degree cup products on a suspension vanish
items.statement: For a nonempty CW complex X and its two-cone unreduced suspension Sigma X, every product of two positive-degree reduced classes over a commutative unital ring is zero; cup-length is at most 1.
items.strategy: Cover Sigma X by its two contractible cone neighborhoods U,V. Homotopy invariance and the direct cochain calculation for a point make their positive-degree cohomology zero. Exactness therefore lifts the two factors to H^*(Sigma X,U) and H^*(Sigma X,V). Their relative product lies in H^*(Sigma X,U union V)=H^*(Sigma X,Sigma X)=0 and maps to the absolute product.

references.title: Hatcher relative cup method §3.2; Miller Lectures 28--29

title: Cup Cap Cross Products and Cohomology Rings — Examples

items.title: Integral cohomology ring of a torus
items.statement: For T^2=S^1 times S^1, H^*(T^2;Z) is the exterior algebra Lambda_Z(x,y), with |x|=|y|=1, x^2=y^2=0, xy=-yx, and xy the positive degree-two generator for the product orientation.
items.strategy: UCT gives H^0(S^1)=H^1(S^1)=Z and no other groups. Kunneth sends the two factor generators to x,y and their tensor to xy. Dimension forces both squares to vanish; the tensor-ring Koszul sign gives yx=-xy. AC is inherited only from the current UCT/Kunneth suppliers.

items.title: Integral cohomology ring of a closed orientable surface
items.statement: For the closed oriented genus-g surface Sigma_g there are degree-one classes a_i,b_i and an oriented generator omega in degree two such that a_i cup b_j=delta_ij omega, b_j cup a_i=-delta_ij omega, all a_i cup a_j and b_i cup b_j vanish, and all products with omega in positive degree vanish.
items.strategy: Use the standard one-vertex CW polygon with oriented edges a_i,b_i and one two-cell attached by the word product [a_i,b_i]. Its cellular homology and UCT give H^1=Z^{2g}, H^2=Z. Triangulate the polygon from the vertex and evaluate the front/back cup formula on the signed two-chain: only the ordered a_i,b_i crossing contributes +1; disjoint/equal edge pairs cancel. Graded commutativity supplies reversed products, and dimension kills products involving omega. AC is inherited only from the current UCT supplier.

items.title: Mod-two cohomology ring of real projective space
items.statement: For n>=0, H^*(RP^n;F_2)=F_2[x]/(x^{n+1}) with |x|=1; restriction RP^n to RP^m carries x to x for m<=n.
items.strategy: Use the standard one-cell-in-each-dimension CW structure. The lift of each attaching map to the sphere has incidence degree 1+(-1)^k, so the integral cellular differential is 2 in even positive degrees and 0 in odd degrees. Cellular comparison and the finite-field UCT give one F_2 in degrees 0..n. For i+j=n, embed RP^i and RP^j as complementary coordinate projective subspaces meeting at one point p. Excision and the explicit deformation retractions of their complements identify their generators with the local classes of the coordinate factors R^i,R^j in the affine chart at p. Relative Kunneth sends their cross product to the local top generator, so naturality makes every x^n nonzero. Restriction and dimension give the truncated polynomial ring. AC is inherited from the current finite-field cohomology/Kunneth suppliers.

items.title: Integral cohomology ring of complex projective space
items.statement: For n>=0, H^*(CP^n;Z)=Z[u]/(u^{n+1}) with |u|=2, normalized so u evaluates as +1 on CP^1 with its complex orientation; restriction CP^n to CP^m preserves u.
items.strategy: The standard CW structure has one cell in each even dimension through 2n and none in odd dimensions, so its cellular boundary is zero. Cellular comparison and UCT give one Z in each even cohomological degree through 2n. Repeat the complementary-coordinate-subspace proof for CP^i,CP^j inside CP^{i+j}: they meet in one point, their complements deformation retract onto the preceding projective subspaces, and the affine chart is C^i times C^j with product complex orientation. Excision and relative Kunneth therefore make the cup of generators a top generator. Induction yields u^k nonzero and normalized positively; restriction and dimension give the quotient. AC is inherited only from the current UCT and Kunneth suppliers.

items.title: Cap product on the oriented circle
items.statement: Let z be the positive singular one-cycle going once around S^1 and alpha in H^1(S^1;Z) evaluate to 1 on z. With cohomology written first, alpha cap [z] is the positive generator of H_0(S^1;Z).
items.strategy: Choose the usual single singular loop sigma with coincident endpoints representing the positive class z, and a cocycle representative alpha with alpha(sigma)=1. The cap formula evaluates on the full one-simplex and retains its terminal vertex, so alpha cap sigma is that vertex. The direct H_0 path-component description identifies it with the positive generator; the boundary identity verifies passage to classes. The assumed evaluation normalization removes any need for a prerequisite example-page computation.

items.title: Equal additive cohomology but different rings
items.statement: CP^3 and S^2 wedge S^4 wedge S^6 have isomorphic integral cohomology groups in every degree but nonisomorphic graded cohomology rings: the degree-two generator of CP^3 has nonzero square, while every positive-degree product on the wedge is zero.
items.strategy: The CP^3 calculation gives Z in degrees 0,2,4,6 with u^2 nonzero. Reduced homology of the finite wedge together with UCT gives the same additive cohomology groups. The wedge of S^2,S^4,S^6 is the suspension of S^1 wedge S^3 wedge S^5, so the suspension theorem kills all its positive-degree products. Any graded-ring isomorphism would preserve the existence of a degree-two class with nonzero square. AC is inherited only from the current UCT supplier.

items.title: An additive coefficient group does not determine a cup multiplication
items.statement: The additive group Z^2 supports distinct unital commutative ring structures, for example Z times Z and Z[epsilon]/(epsilon^2). Therefore an abelian coefficient group G alone supplies no canonical pairing G tensor G to G and no canonical G-valued cup product.
items.strategy: Identify the two additive bases. In Z times Z there are two nonzero orthogonal idempotents, whereas in the dual numbers the only idempotents are 0 and 1 (solve (a+b epsilon)^2=a+b epsilon). Hence the multiplications are not determined by the shared additive group. The cochain front/back evaluation requires precisely such a bilinear pairing; no separate abelian-group definition is needed because the two additive structures are displayed explicitly.

items.title: Cochain cup product is not strictly graded commutative
items.statement: On the standard singular two-simplex, there are integral one-cochains alpha,beta with (alpha cup beta)(id_Delta2)=1 but (beta cup alpha)(id_Delta2)=0. Thus strict graded commutativity fails before passage to cohomology, even though the induced ring is graded commutative.
items.strategy: Let alpha be 1 on the front edge [0,1] and zero on all other singular one-simplex basis elements; let beta be 1 on [1,2] and zero otherwise. The front/back formula gives alpha cup beta=1 on id_Delta2, while beta vanishes on [0,1], so beta cup alpha=0 there. These need not be cocycles; the example concerns cochains.

references.title: Hatcher proof of Theorem 3.11 and cup formula

title: Hurewicz Whitehead Freudenthal and Cw Approximation

items.title: Cellular approximation for maps of CW pairs
items.statement: Let (X,A) and (Y,B) be CW pairs and let f:(X,A) to (Y,B) be continuous. If f is cellular on A, then f is homotopic rel A through maps of pairs to a cellular map g, meaning g(X^n) is contained in Y^n for every n. Two cellular maps homotopic rel A are cellularly homotopic rel A after giving X times I its product CW structure.
items.strategy: Induct over relative cells. The image of each characteristic disk meets a finite subcomplex. In a finite target, triangulate characteristic disks and use simplicial/general-position approximation rel boundary to move an n-disk off the interiors of every cell of dimension greater than n, then retract each punctured cell radially to its boundary. The HEP extends the boundary-fixed deformation across the source cell and preserves earlier skeleta. Quotient gluing and the CW weak topology assemble all cells and stages. Apply the same argument to (X times I, X times boundary I union A times I) for cellular homotopies.

references.title: Hatcher Theorem 4.8 and Lemma 4.10; May Chapter 10 §4

items.title: Each homotopy representative is supported on a finite CW subcomplex
items.statement: Every map from a compact sphere or disk into a CW complex has image in a finite subcomplex; every specified homotopy between such maps has image in a finite subcomplex. After cellular approximation a representative of pi_n(X) lands in X^n, but no single finite subcomplex is asserted to contain all representatives.
items.strategy: Apply the compact-image corollary to S^n, D^n, and their products with I. Cellular approximation gives skeletal dimension control. State the quantifiers per representative to avoid an illicit finite-CW reduction for the whole group.

items.title: CW approximation of an arbitrary space
items.statement: For every space X there is a CW complex Gamma X and a map gamma:Gamma X to X inducing a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on pi_n at every basepoint for all n>=1. A CW approximation of a pair can extend a prescribed approximation of its subspace. The construction can be made without AC by indexing attachments by actual maps and actual nullhomotopy data rather than selecting representatives of classes.
items.strategy: Begin with one 0-cell for every point of X and map it accordingly. At stage n attach an n-cell for every actual based S^n-map into X together with its chosen boundary data, ensuring surjectivity, then attach (n+1)-cells for every actual pair consisting of a kernel representative and a specified nullhomotopy in X, killing the kernel. Extend gamma over each disk using the stored nullhomotopy. Cellular approximation shows later higher cells do not alter lower pi groups; compactness makes every sphere or homotopy factor through a finite stage. The same construction relative to Gamma A gives pairs. All index collections are sets and no representative selection is used.

items.title: Absolute and relative Hurewicz homomorphisms
items.statement: For n>=1, h:pi_n(X,x_0) to H_n(X;Z) sends [f:S^n to X] to f_*([S^n]) for the fixed positive orientation. For n>=2, h:pi_n(X,A,x_0) to H_n(X,A;Z) sends [f:(D^n,boundary D^n,s_0) to (X,A,x_0)] to f_*([D^n,boundary D^n]). These maps are natural, well-defined, and homomorphisms; changing the chosen orientation changes both by a common sign.
items.strategy: The pair long exact sequence, contractibility of D^n, and the oriented sphere generator identify H_n(D^n,boundary D^n) with Z and fix the relative fundamental class by its oriented boundary. Homotopy invariance of relative homology proves well-definedness and naturality is functoriality. For addition, factor the pinch representative through a wedge of two spheres/disks; its fundamental class maps to the sum of the two summand classes, so h([f]+[g])=h[f]+h[g]. The relative group claim begins at n=2, where its group law exists.

references.title: Hatcher Proposition 4.36 and preceding definition; May Chapter 15 §1

items.title: The first Hurewicz map is abelianization
items.statement: For every path-connected space X, h:pi_1(X,x_0) to H_1(X;Z) is surjective and has kernel the commutator subgroup. Hence pi_1(X,x_0)_ab is naturally isomorphic to H_1(X;Z). No local simple-connectivity or CW hypothesis is required.
items.strategy: Subdivide a singular 1-cycle and use paths from all its vertices to x_0; boundary cancellation rewrites its homology class as a sum of based loops, proving surjectivity. A singular 2-simplex has boundary relation [01][12]=[02] after conjugating vertices to x_0, so boundaries impose precisely the relations making loop concatenation additive and therefore kill commutators. Conversely the standard square singular 2-chain bounds each commutator. Thus the induced map from the abelianization has an explicit inverse from cycles.

items.title: Cellular reduction for a highly connected pair
items.statement: Let (X,A) be an (n-1)-connected CW pair with n>=2 and A nonempty. It is homotopy equivalent rel A to a CW pair with no relative cells below n; cells above n+1 affect neither pi_n(X,A) nor H_n(X,A). If A is simply connected, the characteristic n-cells freely generate both groups and the relations from (n+1)-cell attaching maps have identical integer incidence coefficients under Hurewicz.
items.strategy: Starting from A, attach only cells of dimensions n and above, indexed by the actual maps and nullhomotopies used in the CW-approximation construction, to obtain f:(Z,A) to (X,A), identity on A. The pair connectivity and the absolute/relative long exact sequences give the lower isomorphisms; the successive n-, (n+1)-, and higher-cell stages make f surjective and then injective in each remaining homotopy degree. Make f cellular and form its relative mapping cylinder W, collapsing every a times I. The pair sequence gives pi_i(W,Z)=0 in all degrees. Extend a retraction W to Z and a homotopy to the identity one relative cell at a time: each extension obstruction is exactly a class in pi_i(W,Z), hence vanishes, and cofibration/weak-topology gluing keeps A and earlier cells fixed. Thus f is a homotopy equivalence rel A, without invoking the later Whitehead theorem. Truncate Z above n+1 by cellular approximation and cellular dimension. With A simply connected, the relative n-cell characteristic maps form a free abelian basis without pi_1-orbit ambiguity. Project each (n+1)-attaching map to every n-cell sphere; sphere degree is both its homotopy relation coefficient and its cellular incidence coefficient, so Hurewicz identifies the two cokernel presentations.

references.title: Hatcher Proposition 4.15, proof of Theorem 4.32, and Lemma 4.38

items.title: Relative Hurewicz theorem in the simple-connectivity range
items.statement: Let n>=2 and let (X,A,x_0) be an (n-1)-connected CW pair with A nonempty, path-connected and simply connected. Then H_i(X,A;Z)=0 for i<n and the relative Hurewicz homomorphism pi_n(X,A,x_0) to H_n(X,A;Z) is an isomorphism. For n=2 the hypotheses make the relative group abelian; without trivial pi_1(A)-action the general theorem requires a quotient and is not asserted here.
items.strategy: Apply the cellular reduction lemma. With no relative cells below n the cellular complex vanishes below n, and both pi_n and H_n are the cokernel of the same degree-incidence map from the free (n+1)-cell group to the free n-cell group. Hurewicz sends characteristic disks to cellular generators, hence induces the identity on cokernels. The CW-pair hypothesis avoids a circular appeal to weak-equivalence invariance of homology.

references.title: Hatcher Theorem 4.32 and proof; May Chapter 15 §1

items.title: Absolute Hurewicz theorem at the first nonzero degree
items.statement: If a CW complex X is (n-1)-connected, then reduced H_i(X;Z)=0 for i<n. For n>=2, h:pi_n(X) to H_n(X;Z) is an isomorphism. For n=1 and path-connected X, h is abelianization as stated separately. The same conclusions transfer to spaces already known homotopy equivalent to CW complexes.
items.strategy: For n>=2 apply the relative theorem to the CW pair (X,{x_0}); relative homotopy is absolute and relative homology is reduced. Use the degree-one proposition for n=1. Actual homotopy equivalences transport both theories, but a bare weak CW approximation is not used to infer homology invariance.

references.title: Hatcher Theorem 4.32; May Hurewicz Theorem, Chapter 15 §1

items.title: Homotopy excision
items.statement: Let X=A union B be a CW complex, with A,B subcomplexes and nonempty path-connected C=A intersection B. If (A,C) is m-connected and (B,C) is n-connected, m,n>=0, then pi_i(A,C) to pi_i(X,B) is an isomorphism for i<m+n and a surjection for i=m+n, at every basepoint in C.
items.strategy: Cellularly approximate a relative disk in (X,B), put it in general position with respect to cells, and subdivide the domain so inverse images of A and B form labelled regions. Because the two relative connectivities kill labelled regions of dimensions <=m and <=n, successively engulf and remove intersections until, below total dimension m+n, the disk is homotopic rel boundary into A; at the endpoint dimension the same procedure gives existence but not uniqueness. Applying it to a nullhomotopy proves injectivity one degree lower. The proof is relative throughout and compactness reduces each representative to finitely many cells.

references.title: Hatcher Theorem 4.23 and full proof; May Chapter 11 §§1--3

items.title: Blakers--Massey connectivity for a homotopy-pushout square
items.statement: Consider a homotopy-pushout square of based CW complexes with initial maps f:A to B m-connected and g:A to C n-connected, m,n>=1. If P is its homotopy pushout, the canonical map A to the homotopy pullback B times^h_P C is (m+n-1)-connected. Equivalently the square is (m+n-1)-cartesian. The canonical comparison starts at A, not at P.
items.strategy: Replace f,g by mapping-cylinder cofibrations, so P is the ordinary union B union_A C. A point of the homotopy pullback is a pair of endpoints with a path in P; its homotopy fibre over A identifies, via path lifting, with the triad obstruction measured by pi_i(B,A) to pi_i(P,C). Homotopy excision makes that comparison an isomorphism below m+n and surjective at m+n. The fibration long exact sequence shifts this to vanishing homotopy fibres through degree m+n-2, exactly (m+n-1)-connectivity of A to the pullback.

references.title: Hatcher Theorem 4.23; May Homotopy Excision, Chapter 11

items.title: Freudenthal suspension theorem
items.statement: If X is an (n-1)-connected based CW complex with n>=1, suspension pi_i(X) to pi_{i+1}(Sigma X) is an isomorphism for i<2n-1 and a surjection for i=2n-1. Sigma is the two-cone suspension and the map is the usual pinch/adjunction suspension.
items.strategy: Decompose Sigma X=C_+X union C_-X with intersection X. Each cone is contractible, so the pair (C_+X,X) and its negative analogue are n-connected by the pair LES. Identify pi_i(X) with pi_{i+1}(C_+X,X) and pi_{i+1}(Sigma X) with pi_{i+1}(Sigma X,C_-X). Homotopy excision is an isomorphism when i+1<2n and surjective at i+1=2n, giving the exact printed bounds.

items.title: Weak homotopy equivalence
items.statement: A continuous map f:X to Y is a weak homotopy equivalence if pi_0(f) is bijective and, for every x in X and n>=1, f_*:pi_n(X,x) to pi_n(Y,f(x)) is an isomorphism. This includes all components and all source basepoints; it is not defined merely by choosing one basepoint.
items.strategy: This records the exact Whitehead hypothesis. Basepoint-change isomorphisms show that on each path-connected component it is enough to check one source basepoint, but the definition avoids silently omitting components.

items.title: A weak equivalence has vanishing mapping-cylinder relative groups
items.statement: If f:X to Y is a weak homotopy equivalence, then for its mapping-cylinder inclusion j:X to M_f, every relative pi_n(M_f,X,x) is trivial for n>=1 and pi_0(X) to pi_0(M_f) is bijective. Conversely these conditions imply that f is a weak equivalence.
items.strategy: The target deformation retracts onto M_f, so f_* is the inclusion map in the pair LES followed by an isomorphism. Exactness converts isomorphisms on adjacent absolute groups and components into trivial relative groups. The converse follows by reading the same exact sequence in the reverse direction, including its pointed-set tail.

items.title: Vanishing relative homotopy extends an inverse over cells
items.statement: Let i:X to Z be a cellular inclusion of CW complexes with all relative homotopy groups trivial and a component bijection. Then the identity of X extends skeleton by skeleton to r:Z to X, together with a homotopy i r homotopic to id_Z rel X; also r i=id_X. The construction works for arbitrary cell sets and unbounded dimension.
items.strategy: On each n-cell, the already-defined boundary map and homotopy form a relative n-disk in (Z,X). Relative vanishing compresses it into X, supplying both the extension of r and the disk homotopy. Do all cells of a fixed skeleton independently; quotient gluing and the CW weak topology give continuous maps. Cofibration keeps earlier skeleta fixed. The colimit of compatible stages yields r and the homotopy without assuming finitely many cells.

references.title: Hatcher Lemma 4.6 and Theorem 4.5; May HELP theorem

items.title: Whitehead theorem
items.statement: Every weak homotopy equivalence f:X to Y between CW complexes is a homotopy equivalence.
items.strategy: Replace f by the source inclusion into M_f; the target Y is a strong deformation retract of M_f. The relative-vanishing lemma verifies the hypotheses of the extension lemma, which gives X as a deformation retract up to homotopy of M_f. Compose its inverse with the target retraction/inclusion maps to obtain two-sided homotopy inverses for f.

references.title: Hatcher Theorem 4.5; May Whitehead Theorem, Chapter 10 §3

items.title: A weakly contractible CW complex is contractible
items.statement: A nonempty CW complex with one path component and pi_n(X,x)=0 for every n>=1 is contractible.
items.strategy: The unique map X to a point is a weak equivalence by the hypotheses. Both spaces are CW complexes, so Whitehead makes it a homotopy equivalence, exactly a contraction of X.

references.title: Hatcher Whitehead theorem consequence; May Chapter 10 §3

title: Hurewicz Whitehead Freudenthal and Cw Approximation — Examples

items.title: First nonzero homotopy group of a sphere
items.statement: For n>=1, pi_i(S^n)=0 for 0<i<n and pi_n(S^n) is isomorphic to Z. Under Hurewicz the identity sphere map goes to the positive fundamental class, so this is the degree isomorphism.
items.strategy: For n>=2 the sphere is (n-1)-connected and its first reduced homology is Z in degree n, so absolute Hurewicz gives the result. For n=1 use the degree-one abelianization together with pi_1(S^1)=Z, or the already published degree classification. Naturality identifies h with degree.

items.title: Hurewicz calculation for a wedge of simply connected spheres
items.statement: For n>=2 and a nonempty finite set J, X=wedge_{j in J} S^n is (n-1)-connected and pi_n(X) is the free abelian group direct-sum_J Z generated by the wedge inclusions.
items.strategy: The CW structure has one vertex, no cells in dimensions 1 through n-1, and one n-cell per summand, so cellular approximation gives (n-1)-connectivity. Its cellular boundary is zero and H_n is direct-sum_J Z. Hurewicz is natural and sends each sphere inclusion to its cellular generator.

items.title: A simply connected CW homology equivalence is a homotopy equivalence
items.statement: If f:X to Y is a map of simply connected CW complexes inducing isomorphisms on all integral homology groups, then f is a homotopy equivalence.
items.strategy: Replace f by X included in M_f. The homology pair LES makes every H_i(M_f,X) zero, and simple connectivity makes the relative pi_1 trivial. If some higher relative pi_n were first nonzero, the pair would be (n-1)-connected and relative Hurewicz would identify it with the zero H_n, a contradiction. Thus all relative homotopy groups vanish, f is a weak equivalence, and Whitehead applies.

items.title: Freudenthal stable range for spheres
items.statement: For n>=1, suspension pi_i(S^n) to pi_{i+1}(S^{n+1}) is an isomorphism for i<2n-1 and a surjection for i=2n-1. In particular pi_{n+k}(S^n) stabilizes under suspension once n>k+1.
items.strategy: S^n is (n-1)-connected, so substitute X=S^n in Freudenthal and use Sigma S^n homeomorphic to S^{n+1}. Writing i=n+k, the isomorphism condition n+k<2n-1 rearranges to n>k+1; equality gives only the endpoint surjection.

items.title: Whitehead theorem fails without CW type
items.statement: Let Q_d be the rational numbers with the discrete topology and Q the rational subspace of R. The identity set map f:Q_d to Q is a weak homotopy equivalence but not a homotopy equivalence. Thus a CW-type hypothesis cannot be omitted from Whitehead's theorem.
items.strategy: Every path in Q is constant because a connected subset of Q with two points would contain an irrational real between them; hence both spaces have singleton path components and all higher homotopy groups vanish, so f is weak. If g were a homotopy inverse, any homotopy in Q is pointwise constant, forcing f g=id_Q and hence g to be the set-theoretic identity Q to Q_d. This is not continuous since singleton preimages are not open in Q. Q cannot have CW type either, since otherwise Whitehead applied to a CW approximation would force the contradiction.

references.title: May Whitehead theorem hypotheses, Chapter 10 §3; explicit rational-space witness checked locally

items.title: A homology equivalence need not be a homotopy equivalence without simple connectivity
items.statement: Let X be the CW complex with one vertex, one-cells a,b, and one two-cell attached by a^2 b^{-3}. The map f:S^1 to X represented by the loop a b^{-1} is an integral homology equivalence but not a homotopy equivalence.
items.strategy: The cellular complex is 0 to Z --(2,-3)--> Z^2 to Z to 0. The boundary is injective and (x,y) maps to 3x+2y identifies its cokernel with Z; the loop ab^{-1} maps to 1, so f is an isomorphism on H_1 and also on H_0, with all other reduced groups zero. Van Kampen gives pi_1(X)=<a,b | a^2=b^3>, which maps onto nonabelian S_3 via a=(12), b=(123). Since pi_1(S^1)=Z is abelian, f cannot induce an isomorphism on pi_1 and cannot be a homotopy equivalence.

references.title: Hatcher discussion after Corollary 4.33; explicit two-cell witness checked locally
